title: Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation
main_claim: Let f:U->V be a projective surjective morphism with connected fibers between smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, with kbar(V)>=0 and geometric generic fiber F. Then kbar(U) >= kappa(F) + max{kbar(V), Var(f)}, where Var(f) is the birational field-of-definition variation of the whole geometric generic fiber. This is Popa's Conjecture 3.8, and it implies the projective Iitaka-Viehweg C^+ inequality in all dimensions.

issues.description: The whole argument depends on two results imported from the companion 'Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity'. The first is reduced-SNC logarithmic subadditivity in full generality, i.e. the log Iitaka C_{n,m} conjecture (Cor. 6.2). The second is the full-period adjoint comparison (Thm. 3.1). Both are major claims that were not audited here. The main theorem is proved only modulo them. There is no circularity: the companion lists this paper as a downstream user and says it does not use it.
issues.evidence: 'Apply \cite[\PoneLog]{SubadditivityCompanion}' ; 'This is \cite[\PoneAdjoint]{SubadditivityCompanion}, whose proof uses the full period image and boundary numerical-rank loss.'

issues.description: The extension step maps the constructed weights onto conditions (19)-(23) of DHP13 Theorem 4.1. I checked the weight identities themselves: |s_S|^2 e^{-phi_S} <= e^{-1} follows from phi >= log|s_{R_0}|^2, the curvature differences are nonnegative, and the integrability of u^m against phi_{F'} holds. I did not compare this against the exact wording of DHP's hypotheses, especially (22), the domination of the singularities of phi_S, which the paper restates in its own form.
issues.evidence: 'We now extend a nonzero power of u using \cite[Theorem~4.1, conditions~(19)--(23)]{DHP13}. We record every hypothesis in this application.'

coverage:
Read Sections 1-7 in full, plus the 04-constancy-estimates sub-file. I checked these steps in detail:
- Construction of the parameter field: the contraction of xi, Pluecker-ratio constancy of the normal map, rank p_1 of the Hilbert parameter map, C(S)=C(Y) and dim Z = d + dim T_0.
- Root-cover lemma: the Kummer degree and h^0(mK)=1 via the injection into O(2m pi^*E).
- Divisorial normalization: 0<=B_P<=1, B>=D_W^0, and the zero-coefficient corollary.
- Hodge order: the integrability threshold equals 1+a, so a = lambda_P - 1 and T ~ B+M.
- The transfer bound, weak-positivity addition (Fujino) and the interpolation contradiction that gives M|W_z ~ 0.
- Flatness, and finite character via Deligne.
- Analytic constancy criterion: the Atiyah lifting via the pairing identity; I re-derived the recurrence and leading-term formula in cc:zeros. Also the Lelong/integrability lemma with leafwise constancy, the L^{2/k} minimizer argument (curvature of Phi, the adjoint L^2 bound, leading-coefficient preservation, the Hoelder/Markov strict gain), the pole-divergence estimate, BCHM contraction and flows of the regular derivation.
- Markings: the KP model-pair argument, the upper bound d, and the multiplicity-one minimizer at moving tests.
- Descent: Hanamura cocycle averaging in the uniquely divisible quotient, the ramification formulas (re-derived), uniqueness of the special-fiber minimizer, the inertia equality forcing trivial inertia, then purity and Landesman descent of the etale cover.
Not audited: the companion papers, and Sections 8-9, which the paper says the main theorem does not depend on.
